state.asserts: the rung WORKS: implemented, parity-passed, engaging the claimed composition
state.binding: scripts/generate-memory-matrix.mjs#calibrationBinding — envelope membership, because whether a rung executes does not depend on the resolution it executed at

memoryCharacterization.asserts: the rung's PEAKS are known across the geometry envelope
memoryCharacterization.binding: scripts/generate-memory-matrix.mjs#memoryCharacterization — distinct measured geometries, because `fixedGb + perMpxGb * megapixels` has two coefficients and one point cannot determine a slope

conformanceStates.definition: Implemented AND carrying at least one eligible current-environment calibration record. Says nothing about geometry coverage — read `memoryCharacterization` for that.

Implemented and production-admissible for an exact base-only coordinate through a current runtime_complete record. This is intentionally below Full Verified: lifecycle recovery and measured negative-mutation coverage remain owned by the catalog story.
The code path exists and is statically evidenced; no current measurement binds it.
The rung cannot apply to this architecture; there is nothing to measure.
No implementation of this rung on this route.
The route itself does not resolve.

memoryCharacterizationStates.definition: No geometry has been measured for this cell.
Exactly one measured geometry. The peak is known AT that geometry and the slope is undeterminable, so nothing is known about the rest of the envelope.
Two or more distinct measured geometries — sufficient to determine the affine curve, which is not a claim that a fit has been performed. `coveredPixelBound` is the largest measured area.

summary.publicationPredicate: A coordinate is published when it is PLANNED (an entry in config/memory-calibration-plan.json targets it), MEASURED (memoryCharacterization is not `unmeasured`), BOUND to a calibration record in docs/generated/memory-calibration-evidence.json, or CITES evidence of its own (historical, current-environment, strategy-parameter, or structural). Every elided coordinate is therefore unplanned, unmeasured, unbound and uncited; its `state` and its per-rung population are counted in `summary.elidedByState` and `coverage`, never dropped.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: Same uniform 12-block dual-stream trunk as the MLX twin. Mage now drives that trunk through the shared Candle block-window backend for every shipped Candle route without an overlay.
One uniform 12-block dual-stream stack. Windowable in principle; the smallest N in the catalog, so the ceiling on the saving is the lowest.
findings: N = 12 is the smallest uniform stack surveyed. A window of 1 bounds trunk weights at 1/12, against ~1/30 on z-image and ~1/60 on Qwen-Image — applicable, but the least leverage per unit of re-materialization cost.

Mage-Flow is TE-heavy: the conditioning encoder is a full decoder stack of its own (text_encoder/layer.rs). A Dit-scoped window bounds only the 12-block trunk, so the component scope, not the window size, is the parameter that decides whether rung 4 is worth anything here.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: Candle windows the 30-block packed or dense main DiT and the 15-block Fun-Controlnet Union branch through the shared block-window primitive; each 2-block refiner remains resident. Packed-tier LoRA residual plans are retained and replayed onto every materialized main block, so none, LoRA, and strict-control overlays all expose the same request-scoped rung.

The shipped rung-4 exemplar, and still partial: the base DiT is three stacks (2 noise refiners, 2 context refiners, 30 unified layers) and only the 30-layer stack is windowed. The control route adds two more — a 15-block control stack, which IS windowed, and a 2-block control refiner, which is not. The refiner blocks stay resident either way.
findings: The window size is INERT above 1 on this family: 30/15/8/4/2 all land on the same peak and an all-covering attribution control matches window 8 exactly, so `TRANSFORMER_WINDOW_SIZES` publishes [1] rather than a ladder.

Component scope and streamability are two different levers and must not be conflated. Making the encoder streamable at all under Sequential is what let bf16 fit 8 GB (conditioning 8.489 -> 2.718 GiB); the tunable TextEncoder scope cuts conditioning a further 46.5% and moves the request peak 0.0%, which is why the published default is Dit — see gen-core's memory_strategy prerequisite note.

Overlays are compatible here, in contrast to Krea/Candle: adapters are installed as forward-time residuals and `BlockAdapters` replays the captured list onto each materialized block, so a LoRA-carrying request can still stream.

The declaration is per LOAD, and the matrix has no load-source axis. Rung 4 is Missing for a single-file / ComfyUI load, because streaming rebuilds blocks from the snapshot per window and an in-memory `Weights` has no re-openable source. Every catalog route here is a `WeightsSource::Dir` registry load, so the cells are right for the routes the matrix covers — but a consumer must not read them as covering a user-imported single-file checkpoint.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The Candle/CUDA provider reopens the uniform 60-block base/edit DiT from dense mmap tensors or content-addressed packed sidecars and materializes exact shared block windows. The head and tail remain resident. Adapter-bearing requests, including Lightning's built-in LoRA, retain the established additive/folded path and report rung 4 Missing.
findings: Head-once/tail-tiled VAE decode exposes 768, 640, 512, 448, 384, 320, and 256 output-pixel tile edges at overlap 64. Overlap 96 remains only the rejected sub-512 experiment arm.
Lightning and all user-adapter requests preserve their pre-story semantics through the existing additive/folded path and do not inherit the no-overlay rung-4 claim.
The five-block control branch and PiD decoder remain explicit exclusions rather than being inferred from the family-level base implementation.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The shared block-window primitive rebuilds the uniform 60-block base/edit DiT one block at a time for BF16, packed Q4/Q8, and captured LoRA/LoKr residuals. The optional five-block control side branch is structurally windowable but is not implemented by this MLX provider path, so the distinct qwen_image_control provider does not advertise rung 3 or 4.
findings: The five-block QwenFunControlBranch is structurally windowable because it is the same uniform QwenTransformerBlock stack, but the MLX control provider does not implement its block stream in this change. It is a real resident remainder, and qwen_image_control is excluded from rung 3/4 instead of inheriting a family-level claim.

Window 1 is the sole bounded production cadence. The same-stream window-60-versus-window-1 attribution control did not move the conditioning-bound request peak, while the authoritative complete rung-3-versus-rung-4 requests moved the peak by 75.02% for BF16, 52.90% for Q4, and 63.76% for Q8.
The Q4 and Q8 rung-4 captures passed output-equivalence thresholds, range verification, loadability, cleanup, cancellation/error-path scenarios, and the required negative mutation check.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: Both Candle Lens providers expose the uniform 48-block DiT through the shared block-window driver for exact packed q4/q8, deferred, no-overlay loads. Device-format sidecars are prepared outside the measured request and each selected window transfers only its packed blocks to CUDA.
findings: The q4 implementation run is entry-, tier-, mode-, overlay-, geometry-, batch-, and step-specific. It does not certify q8, bf16, base `lens`, style variation, adapters, or a reusable fit.
Base `lens` Candle model-cell ownership belongs to SC-17489 and remains Missing until that story supplies authoritative calibration. SC-15874 retains Lens-Turbo entry-level calibration ownership.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The pinned provider now exposes two distinct measured Lens identities. Base `lens` Q4 uses the full shared ladder and rebuilds both the 24-layer gpt-oss encoder and 48-block DiT with window 1. `lens_turbo` BF16 retains the earlier text-encoder-only window-1 contract. The entry/tier cross-products, adapters, PiD, eager loads, and other numeric tiers remain outside both contracts.
findings: The gpt-oss encoder is MoE. A window over its layers materializes ALL experts of each layer in the window, not the top-k a token routes to, so the per-block cost of a TE-scoped window is the full expert set — a parameter-sizing consequence, not a blocker.

Dense BF16 conditioning scales with the resident window: 80.098 GiB at 24 layers, 33.136 at 8, 21.271 at 4, 15.340 at 2, and 8.767 at 1. Exact identity held at windows 1, 4, and 24; replacing the 24-layer stack with zero layers changed the output by 1.2079592e4, proving the bound is load-bearing.

Lens does not pad every prompt to one fixed token length. Its harmony preamble is fixed, but the measured prompts produced 121, 141, and 181 tokens; window=1 conditioning peaks were 8.748, 8.767, and 8.807 GiB respectively.

The Q4 result is entry-specific: base `lens` Q4 now has a measured full-ladder request win, while `lens_turbo` Q4's text-encoder-only experiment reproducibly increased the full-request peak and remains Missing.

Adapter cells remain Missing, not Structurally N/A. The provider also rejects PiD for this measured contract, although PiD is a request option rather than an overlay axis in this matrix. The TextEncoder primitive is not inherently incapable of coexisting with either; separate dynamic evidence would be required before broadening the production predicate.

The declaration is per load and the matrix has no load-source or materialization axis. The worker opts only base Lens Q4 and Lens-Turbo BF16 directory routes into deferred materialization; a single-file, eager, or Resident load does not receive either contract.

A second, independent gpt-oss stack exists: `LensReasonerModel.layers` (24) sits OUTSIDE the Sequential seam, which only knows the text and heavy bundles, so nothing on this ladder sheds it. It is LATENT rather than live: `attach_reasoner` has no production callers and the registry path leaves it off, so no catalog route reaches it today. It matters only if a route ever turns it on.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: Same uniform dual-path 42-layer backbone; the Candle provider explicitly declares no sequential-offload capability, so rung 4's prerequisite is absent as well.

blockStacks.name: layers
blockStacks.blocks: 42 (each holding two parallel dense paths, so ~84 layers' weights)

rung4SurveyRows.summary: One uniform 42-layer decoder stack — but it is BOTH the conditioning encoder and the denoiser, and each layer carries two parallel dense paths of which a forward uses one. The stack shape is fine; the two consequences are findings.

blockStacks.name: layers
blockStacks.blocks: 42 (each holding two parallel dense paths, so ~84 layers' weights)

findings: The `TextEncoder` component scope is structurally N/A for this family: there is no separate text encoder. Conditioning and denoise are the same 42 layers, so the scope axis collapses to a single component and only `Dit` is meaningful.

Per-block bytes are ~2x what a forward reads, because both dense paths live in the same layer. A window that opens the layer wholesale materializes the unused path too; a useful rung-4 here needs a path-filtered view, which is a loader parameter rather than a change to the primitive.

The bound must be phase-scoped. Windowing the denoise forward re-materializes the stack once per step; windowing the prefill/think rollout would re-materialize it once per TOKEN. The plan is per-forward-pass, so a rung-4 selection for this family has to name the denoise phase explicitly rather than the generator.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The FLUX.1 schnell/dev Candle lanes rebuild independent windows of the 19 double-stream and 38 single-stream DiT stacks through the shared block-window scheduler. FLUX.1 dev additionally carries one budgeted ControlNet or XLabs IP-Adapter overlay while streaming the base trunk. PuLID, PiD, LoRA, combined overlays, and additional controls remain outside this implementation.
Two uniform sub-stacks — 19 double-stream joint blocks then 38 single-stream blocks. One BlockPlan per sub-stack; the residency floor is one double block, which is the larger of the two block kinds.
findings: Heterogeneity here does NOT collapse the saving, which is the case the story's warning is aimed at. The two block kinds are internally uniform, so windowing each independently leaves a floor of one double block against a trunk of 19 double + 38 single — a large bound, not a degenerate one. The warning bites when a single outsized block sets the floor, which is not this shape.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: Same uniform stack; the Candle provider declares no sequential-offload capability, so rung 4's prerequisite is absent as well.
One uniform stack of Ideogram4Block (34 for the base config, 36 for turbo).
Same five sub-stacks; no Candle block-window path.
Five uniform sub-stacks — THREE 2-block refiners (context, noise, ref-image) then 8 double-stream and 32 single-stream. One BlockPlan per sub-stack; the 6 refiner blocks are the stated remainder.
findings: The refiners are three separate 2-block stacks of two different block types, built whether or not a reference image is supplied. Counting them as one stack understates the resident remainder threefold, which is exactly the quantity a partial verdict exists to state.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The only shipped rung-4 outside MLX Z-Image. `TransformerBlocks::Streamed` materializes each selected window through `candle_gen::block_window::run_windowed` and the shared `BlockWindowBackend` contract.
findings: SC-15958 identified an unbacked declaration before SC-15792 landed. SC-15792 supplied Candle's shared `BlockWindowBackend`, moved Krea's streamed loader onto `gen_core::block_window::run_windowed`, and added parity, mutation, cancellation, error-cleanup and worker-thread coverage; the Implemented declaration is now backed at the pinned inference revision.

Overlay incompatibility here is a property of the ADAPTER MECHANISM, not of the architecture: Krea folds diff-patch deltas into the base weights at load, and a streamed block is rebuilt from the snapshot, so the fold cannot be carried. MLX Z-Image, whose adapters are forward-time residuals, streams with overlays fine. The existing Structurally N/A on Krea's Candle overlay cells is therefore correct and must not be generalised to other families.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The four MLX base descriptors (Turbo, Raw, and both edit routes) rebuild exact windows of the shared 28-block DiT through `mlx_gen::block_residency::run_windowed`. The text-fusion front-end remains resident; pose control retains its separate seven-block branch and contract.
findings: Krea is now implemented on both backends, but the contracts are backend-specific: MLX admits the two catalog entries and every base/edit descriptor at q4/q8/bf16, while Candle remains turbo text-to-image only.

MLX low-rank overlays are compatible. Real LoRA and LoKr A/B runs were byte-identical because the stream captures and replays forward-time residual adapters per block. Dense `.diff`/`.diff_b` patches remain excluded at contract construction because they irreversibly mutate the resident base and cannot be reconstructed from the pristine snapshot.

The MLX pose-control provider keeps its distinct seven-block branch and memory contract; `implementedOverlays` excludes control cells so base-DiT evidence cannot be misreported as control-route rung-4 coverage.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: SC-15831 wires the shared 8-double + 24-single Candle Klein provider through the common block-window primitive while keeping catalog-entry evidence independent.
findings: Sharing provider code does not verify a catalog sibling: the base, KV, and True V2 entries retain separate artifact and calibration ownership (SC-15919, SC-17485, and SC-17486).

rung4SurveyRows.summary: Two uniform sub-stacks — 8 double-stream then 24 single-stream — with shared per-stream modulation held outside both.
findings: Shared modulation is a real difference from FLUX.1: `mod_img`/`mod_txt`/`mod_single` are per-stream, not per-block, so they stay resident across every window. They are small, but a window-size calculation that assumes all trunk weights are per-block will be wrong here.

The KV-cache variant (flux2_klein_9b_kv) retains reference K/V per layer across the forward. That is activation state, not weight residency, so it does not block the rung — but it does mean the rung-4 saving on that variant is a smaller share of the request peak than on the non-KV twin.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: SC-15833 wires the 8-double + 48-single Candle dev trunk through the shared block-window primitive for the exact Q4 base text-to-image route.
The same FLUX.2 double/single topology as Klein, through the same transformer module, but scaled up: 8 double + 48 single blocks, twice Klein's single stack.
findings: The control lane runs the control branch to completion BEFORE the base double-block loop and injects the resulting residuals per block. Those residuals are alive across the whole double stack, so on the control lane rung 4 bounds the base trunk while the branch output stays resident — a stated remainder rather than a blocker.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The Candle provider has the same 19-double/38-single split plus the resident modulation approximator, but exposes neither sequential offload nor a block-window loader.
findings: In scope for epic 15448. The newly visible Candle cells stay Missing until the family loader and authoritative CUDA evidence land.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The FLUX MMDiT skeleton with pruned adaLN — 19 double + 38 single uniform sub-stacks windowed through `mlx_gen::block_residency::run_windowed`, plus a small distribution approximator that feeds every block's modulation and stays resident. All three catalog entries are the same provider route (one architecture, one loader, one contract shape), differing only in checkpoint, sampler default and schedule; every measured number is Chroma1-Base's own, never inherited from FLUX.1 or a sibling.
findings: Pruned adaLN makes this family MORE window-friendly than stock FLUX, not less: the blocks carry no `.norm*.linear` weights and take their modulation as a slice of one approximator output computed once per step. That output is a small resident tensor, and the per-block weight bytes a window must materialize are correspondingly smaller.

Rung 2 is `Missing` on an UNRESOLVED margin, not a clean failure. Tiling the FLUX.1 16-ch VAE decode works and the saving is large (−11.4% to −72.4% of the decode phase across 28 swept geometries at the variant's real 28-step schedule), but the best cell (edge 832 / overlap 256) drifts 53/255 against the 48/255 bar the closest sibling admits — and resampling that one geometry across five production latents gives max-drift 28..82, a 2.9× spread that straddles the bar. Nothing in that supports admission, and calling it a clean rejection would overstate the evidence; resolving it needs a quality methodology (perceptual metric or a family-derived bar) the epic has not agreed on.

Rung 3 is `Missing` on a measured verdict: `sdpa_budgeted_bhsd` reaches both block stacks and both attention sites and saves −2.27% at the DiT seam (7.1679 → 7.0053 GiB, bit-exact), but the seam sits ~12 GiB inside the staged request peak so the REQUEST moves −0.001% — which per the epic is not a saving. MLX's fused SDPA streams its scores (no materialized [B,H,Sq,Sk] to bound), and Chroma's MMDiT mask is a per-query [B,1,S,S] tensor (85 MiB per CFG branch at 1024²) the bounded kernel must narrow per chunk.

The rung-4 scope default is `Dit`, and it is measured rather than inherited — the naive phase probe predicts the opposite. T5-XXL is the largest single component (dense bf16 at 10.15 GiB against a 7.14 GiB packed DiT), which makes `TextEncoder` look obviously right; but rung 1 has already shed it before the heavy phase loads, so a `TextEncoder` window moves the request peak −0.00%. The verdict is coupled to rung 2's: a bounded decode would drop the heavy phase below conditioning and flip the binding scope (Kolors/SC-15521 is the same arithmetic with a different decode).

The cadence domain [1, 2, 5, 10] is published as equal-peak alternatives, not a latency frontier: all four bound the request to 14.6932 GiB, and the ms/step ordering moves with execution-order slots and is unresolvable on this instrument (sc-17679). The default 1 rests on being the tightest weight bound.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: Same SDXL-derived U-Net; the Candle provider declares no sequential-offload capability, so rung 4's prerequisite is absent as well.

blockStacks.name: ControlNet attentions[*].transformer_blocks
blockStacks.blocks: 34 TransformerBlocks across 5 Transformer2D stacks (control route only)

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The SDXL U-Net reused verbatim — eleven Transformer2D at depths [2, 2, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 2, 2, 2], six at depth 10 and five at depth 2, 70 windowable blocks inside a non-windowable conv trunk — PLUS a ChatGLM3-6B encoder that is a uniform 28-block stack of its own. Kolors is therefore the ladder's first family to publish more than one rung-4 SCOPE: `Dit`, `TextEncoder` and `Both`.

blockStacks.name: ControlNet attentions[*].transformer_blocks
blockStacks.blocks: 34 TransformerBlocks across 5 Transformer2D stacks (control route only)

findings: See the SDXL family entry (SC-15525) for why a U-Net is not Structurally N/A here. Kolors inherits that verdict exactly, because it inherits the module — but it inherits NONE of the numbers, because it conditions on ChatGLM3-6B rather than SDXL's CLIP-L + OpenCLIP-bigG pair, and that inverts which phase carries the request peak at several advertised geometries.

Kolors is the first family in the ladder to publish a rung-4 SCOPE domain of more than one value: `transformer_window_components = [Dit, TextEncoder, Both]`. The matrix already carries the scope axis as `transformerWindowComponent` inside `strategyParameters` (and `transformerWindowComponents` inside `publishedRanges`), so no schema change was needed to express it — but this is the first time the domain is genuinely three-valued and the choice is load-bearing rather than degenerate.

The production default stays the TIGHT cadence 1, unlike SDXL's 10, and the `Dit` scope, unlike the `Both` that wins at 512². Both are the provider's declarations; the selector may name any point in the published domains.

Rungs 2 and 3 are `Missing` WITH measurements. Rung 2 is by a wide margin the biggest lever on this family's ladder — at 1024² q4 it takes the whole staged request from 16.0412 → 9.9981 GiB (−37.67%) for +10% wall clock (925 → 1018 ms/step), against rung 4's −7.21% for +4.2× — and it CLEARS the 48/255 inherited drift bar at 1024² (38) and 1280² (26), but FAILS it at 1536² (69) and 2048² (53). `MemoryParameterRanges::decode_tile_edges` is an absolute pixel domain with no geometry axis, so no fixed edge holds a constant tile fraction across a 2× output range; the unlock is tracked as sc-17678. Rung 3 moves the peak 0.00% at both measured scopes — the request (16.0412 → 16.0410 GiB) and the U-Net seam (5.3652 → 5.3652 GiB, reproduced across three runs) — and is not bit-exact (max|Δeps| 3.929e-3, 16/255 of image movement at one step, 212/255 by four). An earlier revision published the seam as +12.54% from an un-warmed control: MLX's first `run` in a process reads ~4.6-4.8 GiB whichever plan it executes.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: Same Large/Medium split; the Candle provider declares no sequential-offload capability, so rung 4's prerequisite is absent as well.

Large and Large-Turbo are one uniform 38-block joint stack. Medium is 24 blocks split into two contiguous runs — the leading 13 carry MMDiT-X second attention and a wider AdaLN, the remaining 11 do not — so the family verdict is partial even though two of its three entries are not.
findings: This is the closest thing in the catalog to the story's heterogeneous-block warning, and it still does not collapse: Medium's two kinds are contiguous runs of 13 and 11, so two plans bound the trunk with a floor of one dual-attention block. The last block additionally drops its context branch (`context_pre_only`), which makes it a one-block tail rather than a third kind.
A single family-wide window size would be wrong here: Large's uniform 38 and Medium's 13+11 split have different per-block bytes, so the window parameter has to be per entry, not per family.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The Candle port retains SANA's uniform 20-block transformer stack, but publishes no sequential-offload or block-window path.
findings: In scope for epic 15448. The newly visible Candle cells stay Missing until the family loader and authoritative CUDA evidence land.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: One uniform 20-block stack with adaLN-single modulation.
findings: SANA's blocks carry a depthwise-conv Mix-FFN rather than a plain MLP. That changes per-block byte counts but not the sequential-stack shape the primitive needs.
The gemma-2-2b-it caption encoder is a uniform decoder stack shared with PiD, so a TextEncoder-scoped window is structurally available for this family too.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The Candle provider has the same uniform 28-block DiT stack, but exposes neither sequential offload nor a block-window implementation.
findings: In scope for epic 15448. The newly visible Candle cells stay Missing until the family loader and authoritative CUDA evidence land.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: One uniform 28-block DiT stack over the original Cosmos key naming, windowed through `mlx_gen::block_residency::run_windowed`. The window is declared per LOAD, not per tier: it needs `LoadShape::DeferredMaterialization` (`streamable`) so the stack was never bulk-committed, and rung 1 engaged in the same request so the released phases are what the bound competes against.
findings: Anima's Qwen3-0.6B encoder reuses Z-Image's decoder block, which is the same module Z-Image's shipped TE streaming windows. A TextEncoder-scoped rung 4 here is therefore the smallest port in the catalog — the block constructor already exists in a streamed form.

The scope is published as `Dit` only, and that is a measured decision rather than an omission: rung 1 already sheds the Qwen3-0.6B tower before denoise, and the 6-block `llm_adapter` conditioner is ~1% of the DiT checkpoint, so a TextEncoder scope's only honest measured value on this family is 0.0%.

Rung 4 is declared per LOAD (`streamable` = `LoadShape::DeferredMaterialization`), not per tier. Anima's only matrix tier today is q4 because the catalog entry has no hosted per-tier download variant — the q4/q8/bf16 matrix is packed on-device by the `anima_quant` converter — so the tier axis of this claim is narrower than the family's real tier surface.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The Candle SDXL U-Net has the same windowable Transformer2D sub-stacks inside a non-windowable conv/resnet and skip-connection trunk, with no sequential-offload or block-window path.

blockStacks.name: conv stem / resnets / down-up skip path

findings: In scope for epic 15448. The newly visible Candle cells stay Missing until per-Transformer2D loading and authoritative CUDA evidence land.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: NOT Structurally N/A. The conv/resnet trunk and its skip connections are not windowable, but each Transformer2D holds a genuine uniform stack of TransformerBlock. SDXL-base has ELEVEN Transformer2D in forward order at depths [2, 2, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 2, 2, 2] — six at depth 10 and FIVE at depth 2 — for 70 windowable blocks in total. `mlx_gen::block_residency::run_windowed` is driven once per Transformer2D at a shared cadence.

blockStacks.name: down/up level 2 + mid attentions[*].transformer_blocks
blockStacks.blocks: 10 per Transformer2D × 6 stacks (down_blocks.2 ×2, mid_block ×1, up_blocks.0 ×3) = 60 blocks

blockStacks.name: conv stem / resnets / down-up skip path

findings: The story's first trap is confirmed against the code and the classification is `partial`, not N/A. Its `[0, 2, 10]` shorthand is right about the SHAPE: the config array is [1, 2, 10], but level 0 is a DownBlock2D/UpBlock2D with no attention, so its entry is never read and the effective depths are 2 and 10.

SC-15525's survey text said SDXL has FOUR 2-deep `Transformer2D` sub-stacks. It is FIVE: the down path contributes two (down_blocks.1) and the up path three, because an up block carries `layers_per_block + 1 = 3` attentions. The full forward-order depth array is [2, 2, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 2, 2, 2] — eleven Transformer2D, 70 windowable blocks.

The skip connections bound the SIZE of the win, not its validity. They keep down-path ACTIVATIONS alive across the forward, and rung 4 bounds WEIGHT residency — so the weight bound over each 10-deep sub-stack still holds; what does not shrink is the activation term it is competing against. The measured wins (−6.97% to −21.40% by tier) are that competition priced.

The rung needs a plan PER Transformer2D, not one per model, and that is what shipped: eleven `BlockPlan`s at a shared cadence. `BlockPlan::new` clamps a window to its stack's depth, so a cadence wider than 2 degrades the five 2-deep sub-stacks to fully resident rather than erroring — which is why the domain is stated once and not per depth, and why 10 is the widest cadence that means anything here.

Rungs 2 and 3 are `Missing` WITH measurements rather than unattempted. Rung 2's tiled decode works and is the family's biggest lever — 19.0032 → 15.8660 GiB (−16.51%) of request peak for ~7% wall clock, isolated decode 14.360 → 11.237 GiB (−21.7%) at edge 896 — but it is withheld on QUALITY: the inherited sibling drift bar is 48/255, and on the production latent the same 1024²/edge-896/overlap-192 geometry drifts 84/255 (the synthetic-latent sweep read 38, which is why the withholding argument had to be measured on production latents). It fails the bar outright at 1280²/1536²/2048², and `decode_tile_edges` has no geometry axis to vary the edge with output size. Rung 3's `sdpa_budgeted_bhsd` reaches every attention site including the IP-Adapter branch, but moves the peak 0.00% at BOTH measured scopes — the request (19.0032 → 19.0032 GiB) and the U-Net seam (6.5868 → 6.5868 GiB) — and is not bit-exact on its query-row axis (max|Δeps| 5.25e-3 at one step; 57/255 of image movement at one step, a different image by six). An earlier revision published the seam as +5.1% from an un-warmed control; warmed, both U-Nets read +0.00%.

illustrious_xl_v1 and illustrious_xl_v2 are `Missing` at rung 4 outright, because q8 is their only advertised tier. The cause is the SNAPSHOT, not the architecture: their `unet/` weights are genuinely packed (u32 codes with .scales/.biases, 3.46 GiB, byte-for-byte realvisxl q8's shape) but their `unet/config.json` ships without the `quantization` marker, so `packed_quant_bits` reads nothing, `needs_load_time_quant` returns true, `load_leaves_blocks_lazy` is false and `streamable` refuses. The rung fails closed, which is correct; the repair is a republished snapshot, tracked as sc-17522.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: Same SDXL backbone and IdentityNet on Candle; no block-window path and no sequential-offload declaration.

blockStacks.name: IdentityNet ControlNet
blockStacks.blocks: 34 TransformerBlocks across 5 Transformer2D stacks (x2 with the OpenPose ControlNet in pose mode)

findings: Pose mode holds THREE networks resident — the UNet, the IdentityNet and an OpenPose ControlNet — and the two ControlNets are 34 transformer blocks each, across 5 Transformer2D modules apiece. On that route the windowable share is a minority of the resident transformer weights unless the ControlNets are windowed too, which is a second family-side port, not a parameter.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The SDXL U-Net verdict, plus two additional resident structures: the IdentityNet ControlNet and the face IP-Adapter K/V pairs installed into every cross-attention.

blockStacks.name: IdentityNet ControlNet
blockStacks.blocks: 34 TransformerBlocks across 5 Transformer2D stacks (x2 with the OpenPose ControlNet in pose mode)

findings: The IP-Adapter K/V pairs are installed INTO the cross-attention modules at load. A windowed sub-stack rebuilt from the snapshot would drop them silently and render an identity-free image with no memory assertion and no compile error, so a rung-4 port here needs the same replay discipline Z-Image uses for adapters.
InstantID is a bespoke route with no normal provider descriptor, so it also has no rung-1 capability declaration to build the prerequisite on.

Pose mode holds THREE networks resident — the UNet, the IdentityNet and an OpenPose ControlNet — and the two ControlNets are 34 transformer blocks each, across 5 Transformer2D modules apiece. On that route the windowable share is a minority of the resident transformer weights unless the ControlNets are windowed too, which is a second family-side port, not a parameter.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The bespoke Candle PuLID route now owns a distinct full-request memory contract and lifecycle while delegating its FLUX.1-dev trunk to the shared staged/windowed reference backbone. The exact EVA-CLIP, IdFormer/CA, SCRFD, ArcFace, and BiSeNet bytes remain resident and are priced as five identity components; only the 57-block DiT is windowed. PiD and every non-identity route fail closed.
findings: Rung 4 bounds only the 57-block FLUX trunk. EVA-CLIP, the 10-layer IdFormer, the face stack, and 20 per-step cross-attention modules remain resident and are explicitly priced, so no saving is inferred from block count alone.

Implementation and loadability do not promote evidence: the shared selector continues to choose resident execution until a current full PuLID identity request is present in the packaged evidence bundle. Base FLUX measurements are a different calibration identity and cannot match.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The FLUX.1 double/single verdict, plus an IdFormer whose outputs are injected at fixed block indices through the whole trunk.
findings: Per-block-index injection is expressible in the primitive as it stands — `run_windowed` hands `apply` the window's `Range<usize>`, so the injector can be consulted by absolute block index inside the window. This is a parameter-threading job, not a change to the primitive's shape.
PuLID is a bespoke route with no normal provider descriptor, so like InstantID it has no rung-1 capability declaration to build the prerequisite on.

PuLID has no residency seam at all: the 57-block FLUX trunk, a 24-block EVA-CLIP tower, the 10-layer IdFormer and 20 per-step cross-attention modules are plain owned fields. Rung 4 would bound the trunk while everything else stays resident, so the share of the peak it can move is smaller than the trunk's block count suggests.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The Candle renderer also switches between two uniform Wan expert stacks during denoise. It publishes no sequential-offload or block-window contract, so the two-stack opportunity is in scope but unimplemented.
findings: In scope for epic 15448. The newly visible Candle cells stay Missing until per-expert streaming and authoritative CUDA evidence land.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: Two uniform 40-block Wan expert stacks, both held resident for the whole denoise and switched between by noise level. Each is windowable; one BlockPlan does not cover the trunk, because the trunk is two models.
findings: Dual residency makes this the largest structural rung-4 opportunity in the catalog after Qwen-Image, and for a different reason: 80 blocks are resident while at most one expert's window is in use at any instant. A per-expert plan bounds each, and the idle expert is a whole model that a window schedule could hold at zero.

The guided-velocity modes run SEVERAL full forward passes per step over different conditioning combos. A window plan is re-walked once per forward, so the re-materialization cost of rung 4 is multiplied by the mode's pass count — a latency consequence to price into the window size, not a correctness problem.

Bernini already loads and quantizes one expert before the next so only one bf16 dequant transient is resident. That is a LOAD-TIME transient bound; both experts are resident afterwards, so it does not overlap with what rung 4 would do.
